about: A web-based editor for viewing, editing and converting map data.

prs.title: CSV import picks the right latitude and longitude columns
prs.broken: With a column like population before lat and lon, the import picked population as latitude, putting places off the map or dropping every row.
prs.changed: Headers that are exactly lat, lon or lng, or start with them, now win over ones that only contain them.
prs.matters: Spreadsheets of places land on the map correctly without fixing the columns by hand.

prs.title: CSV exports keep descriptions and nested properties
prs.broken: Exporting to CSV wrote [object Object] for any property holding an object, so HTML descriptions from Google My Maps were lost.
prs.changed: Such values are now written as JSON text, as the other exporters already did.
prs.matters: A CSV export keeps all of your map data.

prs.title: CSV imports read decimal-comma coordinates
prs.broken: CSV files from European Excel, with commas as decimal points, had every point cut to whole degrees, moving it many kilometres.
prs.changed: Coordinates written with a decimal comma are now read as the numbers they are.
prs.matters: Points from European spreadsheets land where they belong.
